text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-Every third violent crime in Norway is written off by the police, who fail to go after the attacker. But the Justice Department says society must fight violence.
-Norwegian state-owned oil company Statoil meets increasing competition at petrol stations with prices being dumped.

-The University of Oslo is in a decay. Work has been done over the past years to restore the building, but it is still not completed. Jon Lilletun, leader of Parliament's church and education committee, says restoration of the university should be considered a national duty.
-After several calm years the Norwegian foreign exchange market is lively again. Experts believe the crown will grow even stronger in the long term.

-Norwegian investment group RGI is getting nowhere with its request to obtain a fishing license for sea-going trawler American Monarch off the Chilean coast. The Chilean Economic Ministry now says RGI's Chilean subsidiary is taking the matter to court in Santiago.
